answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. A new agent posts a hashed commitment, locks a small bond, and waits several epochs before revealing it, earning nothing meanwhile. An honest newcomer loses only patience, but an attacker spinning up thousands of identities must lock capital in every pending commitment at once. Peers also watch the pulse of each identity: real agents emit varied work over time, while clones fire one synchronized signal. Activity that looks too smooth and velvet across many accounts is flagged as collusion, and those bonds are slashed.
